preview: Aniket Panchal shares his Oracle interview experience for the FTE role consisting of an online assessment and two technical/HR interview rounds.
content: Software Developer Interview Experience Aniket Panchal | B.Tech Electrical 2024 FTE 2024 14 Aug 2023 Oracle Financial Software Services came to our campus to recruit final-year students for an FTE for the position of Associate Application Developer. There were around 192 applicants. Eligibility: CGPA - 7+ | No Backlogs | 12th - 70% | 10th - 70% Branches allowed: Circuit Branches(CS, IT, EXTC, Electronics, Electrical) Round 1 - Online Assessment (10th August 2023) Test was conducted on Hackerrank platform. Test was for 100 min and has 22 questions which were divided into four sections 1. Coding (1): Good subsequences Problem statement: A subsequence of a given string is generated by deleting zero or more characters from string,then concatenating remaining characters. A good Subsequence is one where the frequency of each character is same Eg: word=”abca” A total of 15 non-empty subsequences can be formed. The only subsequence that are Not good are ‘aba’ , ‘aca’ , and ‘abca’ As frequency of a is 2 in all above subsequence and other character frequency is one 2. Aptitude (10) 3. Grammar (10) 4. REST API (1): you will find question here Maximum Transfer All other questions in above link was also asked to different students For next interview round 55 students shortlisted and there were two roles (40+15) I was in first role Interview were in offline mode and before interview starts we had a PPT of company were they introduce about what oracle do,how huge it is all kind of stuff and has small QnA Round 2 - Technical Round -1 (14th August 2023) One by one names for round 1 starts coming on whatsapp group and my name come just in 10 minutes when interview started 1. The interviewer was very friendly and she made me comfortable by shaking hands as I entered the cabin. 2. As I sat she ask me famous question “Tell me about yourself” 3. Then she asked whether I knew C/C++. I answered C++. 4. She then went through my resume and then ask me difference between C and C++ 5. Next question was explain me OOPS I explained classes and object and then explained four pillars of OOPS Tip:When explaining pillars of oops try giving real life example 6. She saw python on my resume then asked me what is difference between C++ and python 7. What is runtime polymorphism and compile time polymorphism 8. Method overriding and method overloading 9. Asked me little bit explanation of operator overloading I explained this with example of complex number where we need to add real part with real and img part with img so we overload + for adding in a such way 10. Then she asked me weather I knew SQL or not and if yes can you write sql query I replied, “yes I know SQL and I can write query”, she then move to next question without further question on SQL 11.Explain what is Normalization ? I explained in depth what is normalisation, why we need It , what anomalies can arise if we do not use Normalization 12. Next question was since you are from electrical why you what to come in software domain 13. She Tell me to write code for reverse a string I first explained her approach and then wrote code on page I felt she was satisfied with code at that time but after interview I realise I have done silly mistake in code 14. She saw internship on my resume and I have worked on Postgres so asked me have you write sql query in it I replied, “I have used ORM for dealing with database” 15. She asked me about my participation in college clubs 16. Asked me that weather I know Java or not,I replied no 17. I have participated in two hackathon then she ask me some questions on it not technical one 18. Lastly, the interviewer asked If I had any questions. (PS. Always ask 1-2 questions that show that you’re interested in the company as well as you get to know about the company and the work they do and their tech stack) This round last for around 15-20 minutes but for some student It was around 30-40 minutes Around 29 students were shortlisted for next round Round 3 - Technical +HR (14th August 2023) Interviewer in second round was very senior in Oracle he said he is working from last 15 years in Oracle and before that he was in TCS But he was very friendly and I felt like it was kind of discussion 1. He scan my resume and he saw I have made three projects then he choose one and then ask me to explain one of my project first I had explained what is my project basically do and then what tech stack I have used 2. Further On that same project he asked me to explained working of project with pen and paper by drawing flow charts , like how data is actually being send what db schemas you have defined 3. I have used cloudinary in my project to store images rather than storing in mongo so he asked me why you have use this cloudinary, so I explained this situations and how images are getting stored in cloudinary and then there corresponding links are storing in mongo database 4. Then he ask me how you have integrated API provided by cloudinary in your code I replied I have used api keys provided by them and used there npm package to do so 5. Then he asked me what kind of keys you have used, I did not get his question but I replied cloudinary provide us two keys one is access key and second one is secret key 6. Further on API keys he asked me why two keys are used ? I don’t know knew the answer for this question so I said “I don’t know the answer sir can you explain me” then he just explain me what can be possible reason for this with public and private key concept. he further continues and then explained me why we need to understand whole working of code or any other library if we are using, what actually happening behind the scene. He said me that as scale and complexity increase we need to think in all ways (For me this round was totally based on my understanding on my project and do I understand some working behind my code and how my oops concepts are clear) 7. Then he asked me what definition for abstraction 8. Difference between abstraction and encapsulation 9. Next he ask me how you are processing text data and your multimedia data in input form for that same project 10. Next he gave me one situation and asked me what you will do in it or what oops concept you will use to solve the problem. You have written code for banks say you have a function in that to deposit cheque in it and further you have requirements from USA or other 2 - 4 countries for that same code but they want some extra functionalities for deposit cheque function how you will do it first I said, “I will use inheritance and solved above problem” 11. Then further said to explained me this with help of pen and paper by drawing interface for same Then at same time I said I will use function overriding for required function i.e. deposit cheque function 12. Asked me how you call a derived class function in an efficient manner since you have so many different derived classes and their respective functions. I said I will use a base class pointer to store the address of the derived class and then with run time polymorphism each function will automatically be called and we don’t need to make separate instances of all derived classes. He was very satisfied with my answer and further he explained me concept of extensibility for above problem 13. Then he ask me do I have any question I asked 2 question for same This Interview last for around 45 minutes and questions where mostly around project and oops concepts On the same day around 6 pm results were announced and 19 students were selected and I was one of them Tips: 1. Make sure you enter with a smile and greet them because your first impression can have a lot of impact. 2. Maintain a grooming standard in the interviews, because it impacts your body language. 3. Stay calm, composed, and be confident because it matters a lot . 4. Prepare the “Tell me about yourself” and a few common HR questions beforehand and don’t try to mug them, just remember key points and tell the answer around it because most of the time we forget the answer that we have prepared . 5. For a DSA Question, try to think out loud and share your ideas with the interviewer. If the question is not clear to you, ask the interviewer to explain it again with some test ase. 6. If you finished writing your code, make sure to dry-run it before presenting it to the interviewer. 7. Try to maintain a smile on your face throughout the interview, that reflects how much confidence you have. 8.Try to give mock interviews before actual one because its give you so much confidence 9.In your preparation when you are solving DSA problems try sometimes to explained that problem to yourself only it will help in interviews 10. Don’t lose hope in rejection. Your rejections are just a redirection.
